videos.name: Declaring a single record
videos.desc: Turn one document into an official record.
steps: Go to an EDRMS compliant SharePoint site. The EDRMS logo shows at the top.
Choose the library, and a folder if needed.
Click Create or upload and choose the file.
Required for Word, Excel and other Office files. Not required for images, video or email files.
Click ⋯ next to the file and select Declare as record.
Choose Yes if a paper copy exists, otherwise No.
Wait for the confirmation message. A lock icon appears on the file.
Switch to the Record Management Review view and check the retention and sensitivity labels.

videos.name: Declaring multiple records
videos.desc: Declare several documents in one action.
steps: Open the EDRMS site and select the library.
Tick the checkbox beside each file.
Each Office file needs a sensitivity label.
Click Declare as record from the toolbar.
Every selected file shows a lock icon.
Check the files in the Record Management Review view.

videos.name: Declaring a centralized email
videos.desc: Declare a record into the central records location rather than the site where it was created.
steps: Select the email or document to declare.
Choose Declare as record, then select the central records location as the destination.
Choose Yes if a paper copy exists, otherwise No.
The record is stored centrally and locked.
Check it in the central location's Record Management Review view.

videos.name: Declaring an email in Outlook
videos.desc: Declare an email as a record without leaving Outlook.
steps: Click the EDRMS add-in button in the ribbon.
Select the EDRMS site and library where the email will be stored.
Choose Yes if a paper copy exists, otherwise No.
A confirmation shows the email has been declared.
Find the email in the selected library in SharePoint.

videos.name: Connecting to the ADB jump host
videos.desc: Web access to the jump host is blocked, so connect through the Windows App.
steps: On Windows, download the Windows App from the Microsoft Store.
Sign in with your ADB account, then go to the Apps tab. The virtual machine (VM) is listed there.
Open the VM and log in with the credential password provided to you.
On the VM desktop, double click Visual Studio Code. Wait for the extensions to finish loading (the left panel will show “Getting Your Connections...” for a few seconds).
Click the PostgreSQL icon (elephant) on the left sidebar. Under Connections > Servers, click the server psql-flex-drm-npr-sea to connect.
Expand Databases > drm-npr > Schemas > public > Tables. All EDRMS reporting tables are listed here (for example, TrackingRecords).
Right click the table you need, then click Script as > Script as Create. A new query tab opens showing the table’s structure (its columns and data types).
Run a query to see the records

In the script tab, write or paste a SELECT query below the script (for example: SELECT * FROM public."TrackingRecords";). Highlight only the SELECT lines, then press Shift+Enter (or click the green Run button at the top right). The records appear in the PostgreSQL Query Results panel at the bottom.

videos.name: Creating a Jira ticket
videos.desc: Jira is only reachable through the Singapore VPN, so connect to it first before opening Jira.
steps: Open your VPN app and connect to the Singapore server. Jira will not load without this connection.
Open your browser and go to the ADB Jira site. Sign in with your account if asked.

Go to the project, then click Releases on the left menu. Confirm the release version you need (for example, R2026.4) is listed. If it is missing, ask the PM (Project Manager) to create it first, because you cannot link a ticket to a release that does not exist yet.
Click the Create button at the top of the page. The new ticket form opens.
Type a clear title in the Summary field. This is the ticket name everyone sees, so keep it short and specific
Choose the matching Component. This tells the team which part of the system the ticket belongs to.
Set Affects Version and Fix Version
Choose the Affects Version (the release where the issue was found) and the Fix Version (the release where it will be fixed or delivered).
Paste the acceptance criteria into the Acceptance Criteria field. These are the conditions that must be true for the ticket to count as done.
In the Assignee field, choose the developer responsible for this work.
Check every field once more, then click Create at the bottom of the form. The ticket now appears in the project and under its release.
